message: In the companion API branch, reopening through one spouse's row stamps only the questionnaire owner, so the other spouse's goal status can stay complete and remain sendable.
dismissalDetail: the goal belongs to the attendee that holds the questionnaire, which is the one Reopen marks; a spouse row has no goal to send

message: The 'gives no missing-inputs tooltip on a reopened row' test asserts queryByRole('tooltip') is absent immediately after hover. MUI tooltips open after a delay, so the test passes even if the !row.questionnaireReopenedAt guard is removed.
dismissalDetail: tightened test assertions can come with the next change to these rows; the guard itself works in the UI shots

message: The 'no missing-inputs tooltip on a reopened row' test hovers the disabled button and asserts synchronously, so it passes even if the questionnaireReopenedAt guard is removed.
With refetchQueries removed, the row updates only from the mutation payload, and no test checks the reopened row's status and chips change in place.
dismissalDetail: the row updates through Apollo's cache from the payload's id and fields, the same way the coach mutations update rows

message: When a closed training is what blocks Reopen, the disabled actions button's tooltip blames missing inputs and costs, and a disabled Reopen item gives no reason.
dismissalDetail: the training's own Questionnaire switch sits in the bar above the table and shows Closed

message: The 'blocks Run & Send on the row while the cohort is missing training costs' test now only checks the kebab is disabled, which is true because the cohort is also closed. The missing-costs path and the questionnaireOpen wiring in GoalsTable have no integration coverage.
dismissalDetail: the missing-costs cohort is also closed in the shared mocks; GoalRowActions.test pins the disabled Run & Send item directly

message: Reopen is gated on the selected cohort's questionnaireOpen, but the API shows the questionnaire when any training on the account list is open, so a spouse split across cohorts can be blocked from reopen in one view.
dismissalDetail: the Admin Table works one training at a time; a household split across trainings is reopened from the row whose training is open

message: The client guesses why the questionnaire is locked from the clock while the API already knows the reason.
dismissalDetail: only the wording depends on the clock; the lock is enforced by the API and the page is read-only either way

message: A household whose goal was sent after the deadline, without a submitted questionnaire, still gets the deadline copy telling it to ask for a reopen the API will refuse.
dismissalDetail: a goal sent after a missed deadline is the MPD team's own action; asking them is still the right next step

message: The sent-versus-deadline split uses the browser clock (DateTime.now()) against the deadline. A client clock running behind shows 'goal already sent' for a deadline lockout, and a reopened household with a past deadline still gets 'Due <past date>. After that you can't change or submit it.'
While the table is loading, canRunAndSend is false, so a sendable row shows 'Needs all inputs and training costs' under Run & Send.
dismissalDetail: the menu is disabled while the table loads, so the text is not seen

message: The new secondary text 'Needs all inputs and training costs' is never asserted, nor that it is omitted when canRunAndSend or sent. The text is the only blocked-reason now that the menu tooltip was removed.
dismissalDetail: with #22, the next change to these rows

message: The questionnaireLocked JSDoc and nearby prose still say lock means past the deadline, though locked now also covers a sent goal.
dismissalDetail: the API type documents both reasons; this prose is a helper comment

message: The sent-lock branch is only tested with a future deadline; a locked questionnaire with no deadline (the other way !pastDeadline is true) is untested.
The '|| sent' in the secondary-text condition is dead, since a Sent row has no action and its menu cannot open.
dismissalDetail: harmless and keeps the condition readable
